title: ISIS Organic
subtitle: From Zero Online Presence to Egypt's Fastest-Growing FMCG Brand in E-Commerce
intro: ISIS Organic is a leading Egyptian FMCG brand with over 40 years of heritage in the organic and natural products space. Their portfolio spans honey, herbal teas, natural water, oils, snacks, and juices — products built for health-conscious consumers and distributed widely through physical retail channels across Egypt. Despite strong retail equity and a recognizable brand, ISIS Organic had almost no e-commerce footprint. The opportunity was enormous. The infrastructure to capture it simply did not exist yet.

sections.heading: The Challenge
paragraphs: When ISIS Organic partnered with Dblshot in April 2024, the account presented a clear set of problems that needed to be solved before growth could happen:
Unoptimized product listings with poor search visibility and weak conversion rates.
A fragmented catalog — only a fraction of their product range was available online.
Zero advertising activity across any marketplace.
Inconsistent purchase order fulfillment, costing the brand sales even when demand existed.
No unified digital commerce strategy connecting platforms.

sections.heading: Phase 1 — Building the Amazon Foundation (April 2024)
paragraphs: Dblshot began by completely rebuilding ISIS Organic’s Amazon presence from the ground up. Every product listing was restructured for search relevance and conversion — copy, keywords, imagery, and categorization all brought in line. A full-funnel advertising strategy was launched simultaneously:
Sponsored Brands: driving brand awareness, top-of-search visibility, and brand store traffic.
Sponsored Products: capturing high-intent purchase searches and converting them to orders.
Sponsored Display: retargeting interested shoppers and defending against competitors.

A dedicated Amazon Brand Store was built to cross-sell products across categories, increase basket size, and improve average order value — keeping the Cost-to-Income Ratio (CIR) efficient even as ad spend scaled.
All advertising budgets and targets were tied to a structured forecasting model, not intuition. Every spend decision was anchored to a projected sales outcome and tracked weekly against actuals.
Result in 4 months: 900% Amazon sales growth. Amazon IDQ Score reached 8/10. The brand went from invisible to category-competitive.

sections.heading: Phase 2 — Full Digital Commerce Takeover (August 2024)
paragraphs: After the Amazon breakthrough, ISIS Organic made a decisive move: expanding the Dblshot partnership to cover the entire digital commerce operation. In August 2024, we took over Noon, Breadfast, and GoodsMart — and spearheaded new platform launches on Botit, Rabbit, and Talabat.
Our approach was structured around five pillars.

sections.heading: 1. The Audit
paragraphs: Before scaling, we ran a deep platform-by-platform audit to map performance by SKU, category, and channel. We identified which products had proven demand but were underperforming due to poor catalog structure and low visibility — rather than any lack of market fit. The audit gave us total clarity on where to optimize, where to scale, and where to shift focus first.

sections.heading: 2. Catalog Strengthening Across All Platforms
paragraphs: Expanded the catalog across all platforms — every product with proven demand was properly listed, optimized, and promoted.
Refined slow-moving SKUs with updated descriptions, pricing alignment, and targeted ad strategies.
Aligned stock availability across platforms to prevent fulfillment failures from costing the brand momentum.
Digitized offline retail winners — products that were top sellers in physical stores but were entirely absent online.

sections.heading: 3. Promotions Strategy — Selling at the Right Time
paragraphs: A seasonality-driven promotions plan was built for the full Egyptian shopping calendar. Every platform received a consistent, coordinated promotional presence during peak periods. Every discount was tied to a commercial objective — not run for the sake of activity.

sections.heading: 4. Demand Forecasting & Fulfillment Coordination
paragraphs: Fast growth creates a fulfillment risk if stock is not planned ahead. We worked directly with ISIS Organic to forecast demand per SKU category, coordinate production timelines, and optimize purchase order fulfillment rates. Fulfillment rates were lifted to above 80%, ensuring the brand had the stock to support its own growth.

sections.heading: 5. KPI Framework & Advertising Efficiency
paragraphs: Clear KPIs were set for every platform: sales growth projections based on historical data, CIR targets to maintain profitability while scaling, and conversion rate benchmarks to surface and fix underperforming areas in real time. Nothing was tracked in isolation — all metrics were connected to a unified commercial view.

sections.heading: Platform Executions
paragraphs: Amazon Egypt & KSA: Full-funnel advertising architecture built on Sponsored Brands, Sponsored Products, and Sponsored Display. Amazon Brand Store launched with cross-sell architecture to increase AOV and reduce CIR. Late 2024, all operational requirements for the Amazon KSA launch were completed — product listings, catalog photography, and a dedicated KSA Brand Store, culturally adapted for the Saudi market.

Noon: Product collection buildout and Sponsored Products campaigns deployed to capitalize on Noon’s daily active traffic. Category-level visibility improvements drove awareness, which in turn generated sustained sales growth.

Breadfast: A strategically placed Homepage Hero Banner promoted selected ISIS Organic products across multiple categories simultaneously. The execution delivered a 40% conversion rate and 28% brand uplift — measurable impact from a single high-visibility placement.

GoodsMart: Dblshot’s internal analysis identified that specific product categories — particularly the Honey range — had significant untapped potential on GoodsMart. A targeted category ad campaign was launched to capture this demand, resulting in significant and sustained sales growth on the platform.
Botit: ISIS Organic was launched on Botit as a new channel, expanding its digital reach and establishing a new revenue stream with a dedicated storefront and product catalog.

sections.heading: Results — A Year of Record-Breaking Growth
paragraphs: 2,740% Amazon YoY growth · 245% total e-commerce growth · 350% Breadfast growth · 140% Noon growth · 477% GoodsMart growth.

Beyond the numbers, the transformation turned ISIS Organic from a brand with almost no digital presence into one of the fastest-growing FMCG e-commerce operations in Egypt — across seven platforms, in under twelve months.

title: Spritz
subtitle: Scaling FMCG on E-commerce
intro: In February 2025, Spritz—a brand specializing in healthy, low-calorie cooking oil sprays—chose dblshot as its partner to transform its e-commerce presence.

paragraphs: Scaling FMCG on E- commerce:
Spritz 410% Growth Story

sections.heading: Introduction: A Fresh Start for a Fresh Brand
paragraphs: In February 2025, Spritz—a brand specializing in healthy, low-calorie cooking oil sprays—chose dblshot as its partner to transform its e-commerce presence.

While Spritz had built a strong offline reputation, its presence on Amazon and Noon was still in the early stages of development. The existing listings and visuals had room for improvement to truly capture the premium quality and health-conscious lifestyle values the brand stands for. This presented an exciting opportunity to refine, enhance, and fully showcase Spritz’s unique value proposition across e-commerce platforms.
Visual & Content Gaps: The brand's digital presence needed a visual and structural overhaul to match its strong offline promise.
Limited Catalog (3 SKUs): Working with a highly focused, small product range posed a unique challenge in achieving an efficient and profitable ad spend-to-sales ratio.
Our mission was clear: Build a strong, sales-driven e-commerce ecosystem for Spritz, starting with Amazon and Noon.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Building the Foundation
paragraphs: The Initial Challenge: At the time of onboarding, the Spritz catalog required significant optimization to meet marketplace standards and drive conversions. Specifically, we identified the following areas for improvement:
Non-Compliant Imagery: Product images were not aligned with Amazon’s strict visual guidelines.
Weak Copywriting: Product descriptions failed to clearly highlight the brand’s unique selling propositions (USPs).
Inaccurate Data: Incorrect product specifications were listed on several SKUs.

sections.heading: The Action Plan
paragraphs: We began by building a rock-solid foundation to ensure every SKU was positioned to convert.
Visual Overhaul: Conducted a professional photoshoot and replaced all non-compliant images with highly optimized, conversion-focused visuals.
SEO & Copywriting: Crafted compelling, keyword-rich product descriptions that clearly communicated the brand's value.

Premium A+ Content: Developed immersive branded content showcasing the core value proposition (a healthy, low-calorie alternative), key benefits, and inspiring lifestyle applications to connect with everyday home cooks.

sections.heading: The Results & Campaign Strategy
paragraphs: This catalog overhaul significantly improved visibility and conversions on Amazon, and these same high-quality assets were seamlessly deployed to enhance Spritz’s Noon listings.

Alongside the catalog optimization, we designed targeted ad campaigns focused on educating the audience, maximizing brand awareness, and clearly communicating Spritz’s unique selling propositions (USPs) to generate strong demand for this emerging product category.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Ads Pilot & Forecasting
paragraphs: With a stronger catalog in place, we moved to test advertising performance. We launched targeted pilot campaigns on both Amazon and Noon to establish accurate baseline data.
After one month of testing, the results proved highly promising, giving us the data-backed confidence to build out:
Quarterly sales and promotions forecasts.
A structured advertising spend plan.
Firm CIR and ROAS targets for the remainder of the year.

sections.heading: Phase 3: Scaling with 360° Campaigns
paragraphs: Armed with this data, we deployed full-scale campaigns across both platforms to maximize reach and drive conversions.
Amazon Advertising Execution:
Sponsored Brands: Leveraged for top-of-search visibility and compelling brand storytelling.
Sponsored Products: Deployed strategically to capture high-intent traffic and drive direct conversions.
Sponsored Display: Utilized to protect brand equity, defend our digital shelf space, and retarget high-value audiences.
Noon Advertising Execution:
Premium Placements: Secured banner placements on Noon’s homepage, including a high-impact Sponsored Display spot directly under the "Best Sellers" section.
Sponsored Products: Executed targeted campaigns to win crucial visibility on highly competitive search keywords.

sections.heading: Ramadan 2025 Strategy:
paragraphs: Targeted strategic seasonal keywords to capture holiday-specific buyer intent.
Maximized exposure across both Amazon and Noon.
Leveraged high-traffic placements to ensure maximum visibility during the peak of the shopping season.
Amazon Prime Day (July 2025):
Executed a tailored Prime Day promotions plan.
Combined aggressive advertising, flawless catalog readiness, and strategic discounts to dominate the category during this critical, high-volume sales event.

sections.heading: The Results: Spritz’s Growth Story in Numbers
paragraphs: In less than six months, our strategic overhaul delivered massive, measurable impact:
410% Overall Growth across Amazon and Noon (Q1 2025 vs. Q1 2024).
275% Sustained Growth across Amazon and Noon (Q2 2025 vs. Q2 2024).
9% CIR (11x ROAS) maintained efficiently across all advertising campaigns.
By executing a data-backed, full-funnel strategy, Spritz evolved from an underperforming e-commerce presence into a high-growth FMCG brand with strong digital dominance.

sections.heading: Expanding Beyond Marketplaces: Website & Social Media
paragraphs: By mid-2025, Spritz’s rapid growth on Amazon and Noon had officially set the stage for the brand's next critical phase of digital expansion.

sections.heading: June 2025: The Website Revamp
paragraphs: We embarked on a full-scale revamp of Spritz’s official online store. By moving from initial wireframes in Figma to a fully optimized WordPress build, we focused on:
Modern UX/UI Design: Crafted to perfectly match the brand’s premium, health-conscious positioning.
SEO & Navigation: Built clear product pathways and optimized on-page content to capture organic search traffic.
Seamless Purchase Flows: Engineered a frictionless checkout experience to boost direct-to-consumer (D2C) conversions.

sections.heading: July 2025: Social Media Activation
paragraphs: To complement the massive e-commerce momentum, we fully took over Spritz’s social media presence to build community and drive top-of-funnel traffic.
Fresh Content Strategy: Developed a cohesive, engaging content plan perfectly aligned with the brand’s healthy-living values.
Thumb-Stopping Creatives: Designed high-quality, dynamic visuals engineered to capture attention in crowded social feeds.
Performance-Driven Campaigns: Launched highly targeted ad campaigns to build brand awareness, foster meaningful engagement, and drive external traffic back to the newly optimized e-commerce channels.
We executed a highly tailored advertising plan, formulated directly from the forecasted spend and sales projections established during our initial "Planning" phase.
How We Leveraged Ad Formats:
Sponsored Brands: Utilized to effectively communicate the brand's core message, increase top-of-mind awareness, and drive sales.
Sponsored Products: Deployed strategically to capture high-intent search traffic and maximize direct sales.
Sponsored Display: Implemented to drive conversions, build broader awareness, and create a defensive moat for brand protection against competitors.
Noon offers a brand store with an annual subscription fee, however there we can always utilize sponsored brands to communicate brand message, as well as sponsored products to drive sales.
Other E-Commerce Platforms: GoodsMart
Based on historical data and dblshot's internal analysis, we discovered that specific product categories had massive potential on GoodsMart but were currently underperforming.

Targeted Category Promotions: To capture this untapped demand, we launched strategic promotional campaigns designed to boost visibility, shift slow-moving inventory, and drive immediate sales on the platform.
A Hero Banner was executed strategically to drive sales on selected products and categories
Internationalization:
A step towards Global E commerce Excellence.

sections.heading: Conclusion: From Zero to a Category Leader
paragraphs: Spritz’s journey shows what happens when a strong product meets a clear digital strategy. By addressing catalog fundamentals, investing in brand storytelling, and scaling advertising with precision, we helped Spritz secure a leading position on Amazon and Noon in less than half a year.

title: Rehana
subtitle: Ramadan Launch Under Pressure
intro: In the lead-up to Ramadan 2025, Rehana — a household name in pantry essentials like rice, vinegar, sugar, and oils — came to DBLSHOT with a critical challenge: make a significant impact on Amazon in just one month.

sections.heading: A High-Stakes FMCG Launch Under Pressure
paragraphs: With no existing Amazon store, a vast catalog of SKUs, and Ramadan right around the corner, we had to move fast. Planning, execution, and results all had to happen within 30 days.

sections.heading: The Mission: Turn Limited Time Into Deep Impact
paragraphs: We began by stripping the project down to its essentials. With time ticking, our first move was to establish a solid performance foundation that could carry the weight of Ramadan’s consumer demand.

sections.heading: Phase 1: Strategic Planning (Week 1)
paragraphs: With the clock ticking, we dedicated the first week to intensive data analysis and roadmap development.
Inventory Analysis: We scanned Rehana’s extensive catalog to identify which SKUs were most relevant for Ramadan and which required strategic pushes to move aging stock.
Promotions Map: Using demand signals and inventory insights, we created a precise promotion plan tied to stock levels, margin goals, and seasonality.
Ads Forecast: Developed a data-driven advertising budget and performance forecast, ensuring every dollar spent had clear ROI targets.

sections.heading: Phase 2: Store Creation (Week 2)
paragraphs: Amazon shoppers don’t just buy products, they explore brands. That’s why a dedicated Amazon storefront was non-negotiable, even with the clock ticking.
Conversion-Optimized Amazon Store: Designed a storefront with a clear visual identity specifically tied to the Ramadan season.
Seasonal Landing Page: Built a dedicated “Deals of the Month” page to house all promoted SKUs for high-impact visibility.
Mobile-First Performance: Ensured seamless navigation across all product categories, optimized for fast, frictionless mobile shopping.

sections.heading: Phase 3: Advertising Execution (Weeks 3–4)
paragraphs: With the strategy locked and the store live, we launched a 360° Amazon Ads campaign designed to reach shoppers at every stage of their journey — from initial discovery to final purchase.
Sponsored Products: Deployed to dominate category-level searches and high-intent Ramadan keywords.
Sponsored Brands: Leveraged to drive brand discovery and encourage cross-selling across the catalog.
Sponsored Display: Utilized for strategic retargeting and category defense.
Video Ads: Funneled high-quality traffic directly to the newly launched Rehana store.
We didn’t just focus on sales — we prioritized visibility, intent capture, and high-velocity conversion.

sections.heading: The Outcome: Ramadan, Won
paragraphs: Despite the tight timeline, the results spoke for themselves:
350% growth on promoted Ramadan SKUs (oils, rice, sugar).
40% increase in total Amazon sales, month-over-month.
40% growth on aged inventory SKUs that were previously stagnant.
Significant uplift in brand visibility and store traffic throughout the season.
In just four weeks, Rehana went from underground to unmissable — right in time for Ramadan’s peak.

sections.heading: Final Word: The Power of Precision Under Pressure
paragraphs: Some brands spend months preparing for seasonal success. Rehana did it in one — with the right team, the right insights, and the right execution.
Whether you’ve got a year or just 30 days to make your mark, we can help you win your moment, too.

title: RAW Kettle Cooked Potatoes
subtitle: 370% Amazon Growth Through AOV Engineering & ROAS Optimization
intro: RAW Kettle Cooked Potatoes is an Egyptian snack brand offering a premium kettle-cooked chip product across a range of flavors. With a quality product and strong brand identity, RAW had the foundations to perform well on Amazon — but was not yet unlocking the full commercial potential of the platform.

sections.heading: The Opportunity
paragraphs: The challenge was not simply driving more traffic or more clicks. It was about increasing the value of each transaction — getting buyers who were already interested to spend more per order. Dblshot identified Average Order Value (AOV) as the primary lever that could transform RAW’s Amazon economics without simply increasing ad spend.

sections.heading: The Strategy — Buy 3, Get 25% Off
paragraphs: Dblshot introduced a bundle promotion mechanic: Buy 3, Get 25% Off. The logic was straightforward — rather than competing on price at the unit level, incentivize multi-unit purchases to increase transaction size, improve ad efficiency, and create a stronger per-order margin profile.

The promotion was introduced as a controlled test. Performance was monitored closely — not just for sales lift, but for ROAS impact and margin health. The results validated the hypothesis immediately: ROAS moved from 2.11 to 5.6 — a transformation in advertising efficiency that made further scaling commercially viable.

sections.heading: Expanding the Model — Bundle Listings
paragraphs: After the promotion performance was confirmed, Dblshot extended the AOV strategy into a structural product listing approach. New bundle listings were created: Box of 3, Box of 6, and Box of 10. This moved the AOV mechanic from a promotional tactic into a permanent catalog architecture — available to all shoppers at all times, not just during active promotions.
The bundle listings also provided a cleaner advertising surface: higher-value SKUs that could be promoted at a competitive ROAS while generating more revenue per click than single-unit listings.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: 370% Amazon sales growth in November — the month of primary execution.
ROAS improved from 2.11 to 5.6 following bundle strategy implementation.
New catalog architecture (Box of 3, 6, and 10) established as permanent SKUs.
Strategy validated and scaled across the broader catalog.

The RAW case demonstrates one of Dblshot’s core Amazon capabilities: not just driving traffic and sales, but engineering the transaction structure itself to maximize revenue per advertising dollar spent.

title: Cimento Força
subtitle: Mozambique Market Entry, Brand & Social Launch
intro: Mapping Mozambique's cement market, building a full brand identity for a new FESCO cement brand, and launching the only fully localized social presence in an uncontested digital category.

sections.heading: The Challenge
paragraphs: Cimento Força needed to build commercial momentum from a baseline that was already in market. The goal was not simply to generate one-off sales lifts, but to build a system that produced consistent growth month after month — through a combination of stronger brand visibility, distribution network development, and customer engagement.

sections.heading: The Approach
paragraphs: Dblshot developed and executed a strategy focused on two parallel tracks: building the brand’s presence and credibility in market, and actively expanding the commercial distribution network — bringing more distributors and contractors on board who would recommend and stock the product.
May established the initial sales foundation and proved commercial viability. From that baseline, the work shifted to compounding the performance:
June: +47% — increased brand presence and enhanced customer engagement drove the first major uplift.
July: +31% — more distributors and contractors onboarded, creating recommendation-driven pull through the trade channel.
August: +30% — consistent execution and deepening market penetration sustained momentum for a fourth consecutive month.

sections.heading: Results
paragraphs: Four consecutive months of growth. Each month building on the last. The Sales vs Target Achievement chart showed month-on-month progression from approximately 2,000 units in May to over 7,000 units by August — a trajectory that demonstrated the compounding effect of building distribution depth alongside brand visibility.

Cimento Força illustrates Dblshot’s ability to operate beyond traditional digital-first environments — applying performance marketing principles to drive measurable, compounding commercial growth in a trade-dependent, emerging-market context.
